svg.title: A Narrowing Auction Cohort
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-02-auction-underwriting-cohort; chart type: funnel; title: A Narrowing Auction Cohort; subtitle: One acquisition cohort, five nested stages, and explicit rejection.; chapter number: 6; epistemic tag: illustrative_model; assumptions note: Illustrative counts represent the same candidate pool, not historical conversion evidence. Every later stage is a subset of the preceding stage. Twenty acquisitions at an average $37,500 all-in basis use the $750,000 acquisition bucket in the $1,000,000 capital illustration; this is not a 30-day target.; caption: Screening automation reduces manual review volume. It does not turn title exceptions into clean assets or convert acquired certificates into certain redemptions.; stages: label: Published sale candidates; value: 1,000 entries form the starting cohort; numeric value: 1000.0; detail: Import 1,000 county sale entries into one dated cohort. Retain withdrawn and duplicate entries as excluded records so the original denominator remains auditable.; label: Desktop-qualified parcels; value: 300 remain; 30% of starting entries; numeric value: 300.0; detail: Retain 300 candidates after removing duplicates, withdrawals, unusable parcel fragments, inaccessible land, and assets outside the selected county strategy.; label: Title-reviewed candidates; value: 120 remain; 40% of desktop-qualified parcels; numeric value: 120.0; detail: Advance 120 of the 300 desktop survivors after recorded interest review, bankruptcy checks, and counsel's identification of the applicable redemption procedure.; label: Price-qualified bid plans; value: 40 remain; one-third of reviewed candidates; numeric value: 40.0; detail: Approve internal bid plans for 40 of the 120 reviewed candidates after modeling premiums, taxes, duration, loss exposure, and portfolio concentration limits.; label: Funded acquisitions; value: 20 acquired; 50% of price-qualified plans; numeric value: 20.0; detail: Acquire 20 of the 40 planned bids without exceeding individual price ceilings. The resulting 2% overall conversion measures purchase selection, not redemption probability or future investment profitability.

rect.title: label: Published sale candidates; value: 1,000 entries form the starting cohort; numeric value: 1000.0; detail: Import 1,000 county sale entries into one dated cohort. Retain withdrawn and duplicate entries as excluded records so the original denominator remains auditable.

label: Desktop-qualified parcels; value: 300 remain; 30% of starting entries; numeric value: 300.0; detail: Retain 300 candidates after removing duplicates, withdrawals, unusable parcel fragments, inaccessible land, and assets outside the selected county strategy.

label: Title-reviewed candidates; value: 120 remain; 40% of desktop-qualified parcels; numeric value: 120.0; detail: Advance 120 of the 300 desktop survivors after recorded interest review, bankruptcy checks, and counsel's identification of the applicable redemption procedure.

label: Price-qualified bid plans; value: 40 remain; one-third of reviewed candidates; numeric value: 40.0; detail: Approve internal bid plans for 40 of the 120 reviewed candidates after modeling premiums, taxes, duration, loss exposure, and portfolio concentration limits.

label: Funded acquisitions; value: 20 acquired; 50% of price-qualified plans; numeric value: 20.0; detail: Acquire 20 of the 40 planned bids without exceeding individual price ceilings. The resulting 2% overall conversion measures purchase selection, not redemption probability or future investment profitability.

text.title: Assumptions: Illustrative counts represent the same candidate pool, not historical conversion evidence. Every later stage is a subset of the preceding stage. Twenty acquisitions at an average $37,500 all-in basis use the $750,000 acquisition bucket in the $1,000,000 capital illustration; this is not a 30-day target.
